form.title: New connection
form.hostHint: Database on this machine? Use host.docker.internal, not localhost/127.0.0.1 — DbButler runs in its own container, so that would point at itself.
form.schemasHint: Comma-separated schema names. Narrows Table Health and every Advisor tab to just these schemas — leave blank to see everything, the default.
form.rolesNote: pg_monitor is enough to watch a database — DbButler never needs superuser. To also use maintenance actions (Vacuum/Analyze/reset stats), the role additionally needs to own the tables, or (PostgreSQL 17+) membership in the built-in pg_maintain role.

card.editSchemasTitle: Choose which schemas Table Health and the Advisor tabs consider
card.removeMessage: Remove "{{name}}" ({{address}})? DbButler stops monitoring it and its collected history is deleted. The database itself is not touched.

pgbouncer.title: PgBouncer (optional)
pgbouncer.description: If this database sits behind PgBouncer, connect to its admin console to see pool utilization on the Dashboard. A user in PgBouncer's stats_users list is enough — this never runs PAUSE/KILL/RELOAD.
pgbouncer.removeMessageNamed: Stop reading pool stats from PgBouncer at {{address}} for "{{name}}"? The Dashboard's Pooler tile goes back to unconfigured.
pgbouncer.removeMessage: Stop reading pool stats from PgBouncer at {{address}}? The Dashboard's Pooler tile goes back to unconfigured.
